evals.prompt: Set up gud so that commits in this repo get AI-generated messages automatically. I already have GOOGLE_API_KEY set in my environment. Don't make any commits yet — just install it, verify it, and tell me anything I should know about how it behaves.
evals.expected_output: Repo-local gud hook installed and verified; report explains that plain `git commit` gets a generated message, `git commit -m` messages are left untouched, and a usable GOOGLE_API_KEY is required or commits with staged changes fail.
expectations: The repo-local prepare-commit-msg hook is installed and invokes the gud binary (the hook file exists in the repository's git dir and calls `git-message hook run`).
The agent verifies the installation before reporting (e.g., inspects the hook file or otherwise confirms it is active).
The agent explains that plain `git commit` gets a generated message while a `git commit -m` message is left untouched.
The agent flags the credential requirement: without a usable GOOGLE_API_KEY, commits with staged changes fail.
No commit is created by the agent (the user asked not to commit).
No global git configuration is changed — in particular no global core.hooksPath is set.

evals.prompt: Every commit in this repo now fails with: `Error: failed to create request client: api key is required`. I don't have a gud API key and I don't want one — I just need to be able to commit normally again. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Agent identifies the installed gud prepare-commit-msg hook as the cause, uninstalls/disables it, verifies that committing works again, and explains the key requirement.
expectations: The agent identifies the installed gud prepare-commit-msg hook as the cause of the failing commits.
The gud hook is no longer active in the repository (uninstalled, removed, or disabled).
Committing works again after the fix — either a successful commit is demonstrated or the repo is left in a state where `git commit -m` succeeds.
The agent explains the root cause: the hook initializes the model client on every commit and needs an API key, even for `-m` commits.

evals.prompt: I want gud to generate my commit messages in this repo. Important: my prepare-commit-msg hook appends 'Refs: AREA-123' to every commit message and I can't lose it. Set it up so both happen — or tell me if that's not possible.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects the pre-existing hook, does not clobber it, and either wraps it with gud (gud first, ticket append second) or flags the conflict for the user; the ticket logic survives.
expectations: The agent detects the pre-existing prepare-commit-msg hook before installing anything.
The existing ticket logic is preserved: the active hook still appends 'Refs: AREA-123' (original file or a wrapper), or the agent left it untouched after flagging the conflict.
The agent does not silently overwrite the existing hook with gud's.
The agent explains how the two coexist (git runs one script per hook name; gud runs before the ticket append) or clearly asks the user how to proceed.
